scoring_justification: The checker recomputes expected dose values from a hidden analytic reference curve and compares pointwise; the optimum thickness is compared with tolerance. The agent's raw CSV is used, not self‑reported metrics.

hidden_assets.purpose: Analytic reference curve for dose vs. thickness and dose vs. voltage, and optimum thickness value (3.0 µm).
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Derived from a correct implementation of the simple ITS model described in the paper for a tantalum foil with normally‑incident electrons and reflex boundary.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Pre‑computed analytic fit to the expected output of a full Monte Carlo simulation using Bethe stopping power and screened Rutherford scattering.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: The curve shape and optimum thickness are physically reasonable and consistent with the paper’s description of an optimum thickness that maximises dose.

outputs.description: Simulated dose per electron at 1 MV for various foil thicknesses, and at the optimum thickness for various voltages. Compared to hidden reference values within tolerance.
Optimum foil thickness in microns at 1 MV. The checker compares this to the paper-derived optimum with an absolute tolerance.

output_contract.notes: The simulation must use Bethe stopping power and screened Rutherford elastic scattering for tantalum. The checker will compare dose values to hidden reference data obtained from a correct implementation of the same simple reflex model, applying a relative tolerance on dose and an absolute tolerance on optimum thickness. Trends (dose maximum, monotonic voltage dependence) are also verified.
